note: How the game finds an inner file of each binder kind (the file name's last extension before .dcx), from the game-model session's survey of about 1,400 vanilla binders across 30 kinds (Elden Ring 1.17.1, 2026-10-12; game-model/missing-files.md). id: the entry ID is a fixed role slot, so inner files are matched by ID (observed in game for partsbnd: renamed mods work; inferred for the others from the same structure). name: the ID is a position (0, 1, 2... or a per-type base plus a position), so adding a file shifts the rest and inner files are matched by name. both: name and ID agree in every vanilla binder (matched by name; a mod whose two disagree is reported). A kind not listed falls back to the game's copy: IDs 0..n-1 in order, or a per-type base plus a position, mean name; anything else means ID. omission: how the build report calls the inner files a mod's copy lacks, and what that does in game. Checked 2026-10-13 against the installed game (read-only, a few binders each): cutscenebnd IDs are cutNNNN x 10,000 plus the clip (they follow the inner path: both) and nvmhktbnd IDs are a per-type base plus a position (name), where the survey's table had ID for both.
